input.summary:
P4 living room (parts/room-30.mjs) furnished inside [68,2,14,71,4,17]: sofa of four stairs along the front wall under the windows, a fence-and-top-slab table with a lamp, two armchairs, a red runner from the doorway lane (z15), a barrel sideboard with a potted poppy, and a standing lantern on the table plus one on the second sideboard.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; my part reports 15 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. Room check on the stub build: 9 floor cells, min light 11, 0 dark, lane z15 clear.
Still open: no floor layer at y1 and no walls yet in this copy, so carpets float and walk/light are only partly verified. Re-run the room check after the shell merges.
left: The floor layer at y1 is not in this copy (shell stub): the three red_carpet cells at y2 (x69..71, z15) show as floating in `$MCD fit` and `check`. They should sit on the shell's floor once it merges; re-run the room check then.

Walkability is not verified: the room tool reports the room unreachable because the shell's walls and floor are absent here. By reading the layout, the z15 lane runs from the doorway at x72 to x69, and both armchairs and the table are reachable from it. The sideboard at (71,2,17) is reached through no free neighbour, but nothing needs to stand beside it.
The room check's light figures (min 11, 0 dark) come from the stub build, where the lanterns are at (70,4,16) and (71,3,17). Re-check after the merge, when the ceiling and walls exist.
The plan's room label says 'floor y=3' but the feet are at y2 (floor layer y1), which is confusing; the plan's room tool should print the feet level.

The elements.md item 'Per house: living room/parlour, kitchen with stove, dining table, bedrooms' is shared across the row, so I did not tick it; plan.md's checklist only covers PARTS 1-6, so no tick was made for part 37.

waste.what: Dumped the blocks in the room box cell by cell with a throwaway node script to see the stair flight and which floor cells were empty.
waste.cost: One script written and run, about 3 tool calls.
waste.tool: `$MCD cells build.nbt --box 67,1,13,72,5,18`, a per-y grid of block ids for a box, would replace the hand-written dump.

waste.what: Worked out the layer rows (x68..71 by z14..17) and the lane and light cells by hand, and checked them only against the room tool's floor grid.
waste.cost: About 20 cells reasoned about and 3 layers written by hand.
waste.tool: `$MCD plan --rooms ... --layers` could print each y level's free cells, so the feet, table and lamp heights are seen without guessing.

waste.what: Could not test the walk or the light with floor and walls present, because the shell is a stub in this copy.
waste.cost: One room-check run that gave an unreachable verdict for reasons outside my part.
waste.tool: A `$MCD room --assume-shell` option, or a fixture copy of the neighbouring shell, would let a room designer test walk and light before the merge.

companions.task: Lay the y1 floor block layer under the living room (x68..71, z14..17) so the carpets have a top face, and check the doorway threshold at x72 z15 is level with it.
Confirm the locked oak stair flight at x68 z15..17 reads as a sofa-side flight with its foot clear, since the sofa at z14 sits at its north end.
